name: Theatre & Performing Arts
purpose: Individually authored episode questions and coverage boundaries for Theatre & Performing Arts. The subject progression is organized by concrete content rather than a topic-by-angle multiplication.

topics.question: What changes when a story is performed for a physically present audience?
topics.coverage: Compare timing, shared space, contingency and feedback through an original scene; avoid claiming that recorded performance lacks artistic value or that audiences respond uniformly.

topics.question: How do proscenium, thrust and in-the-round stages create different visibility problems?
topics.coverage: Use original blocking diagrams with sightlines and entrances; distinguish spatial affordances from a rule that one configuration suits every play.

topics.question: What does a theatre programme reveal about work beyond the lead performers?
topics.coverage: Map credited design, stage management, technical, access and production roles using authorized materials; avoid attributing collaborative decisions to a single celebrity.

topics.question: How can a dramaturg turn research into decisions a production can actually use?
topics.coverage: Develop a bounded source packet for an original scene with context, pronunciation and unresolved questions; distinguish research support from dictating one interpretation.

topics.question: What does cutting a scene change besides the running time?
topics.coverage: Compare information, character relationships and later payoffs in a rights-cleared script; track necessary approvals and avoid presenting altered copyrighted work without permission.

topics.question: How can translating a play affect performance choices beyond literal meaning?
topics.coverage: Compare a short authorized passage for rhythm, address, register and cultural references; attribute translators and distinguish readable text from speakable choices.

topics.question: Why can documentary theatre require stricter provenance than an invented monologue?
topics.coverage: Trace interviews, public records, editing and consent in an authorized example; label composites and do not present invented words as actual testimony.

topics.question: How can an actor pursue an objective without explaining every thought to the audience?
topics.coverage: Use an original scene to compare playable actions, obstacles and observable behavior; distinguish rehearsal vocabulary from claims about a universal psychology.

topics.question: What makes ensemble timing more than performers remembering their own lines?
topics.coverage: Examine cues, listening, rhythm and shared attention in consented rehearsal footage; avoid inferring a performer's private emotions from the result.

topics.question: How can rehearsal feedback remain specific without becoming a judgment of the performer as a person?
topics.coverage: Compare task-focused notes, agreed language and opportunities to clarify in an original example; preserve consent and exclude humiliation as a training method.

topics.question: What should be negotiated before rehearsing physically intimate or violent-looking scenes?
topics.coverage: Use recognized professional standards on consent, qualified coordination and boundaries; exclude combat choreography, coercive exercises and unsupervised imitation.

topics.question: How does stage projection differ from simply making a voice louder?
topics.coverage: Consult qualified voice pedagogy on intelligibility, resonance and venue conditions; exclude strain-inducing exercises or diagnosing vocal health.

topics.question: What can a gesture communicate differently at the back of a large auditorium?
topics.coverage: Compare scale, tempo and sightlines in a documented performance context; distinguish legibility from a universal preference for exaggerated acting.

topics.question: How does a musical number change dramatic action rather than pause it?
topics.coverage: Analyze a rights-cleared example for objective, information, rhythm and transition; separate the book, score, choreography and performer contributions.

topics.question: Why does performing with live musicians require a different cue relationship from a fixed recording?
topics.coverage: Inspect tempo flexibility, conductor communication and technical dependencies through authorized practice records; avoid presenting one company's arrangement as industry-wide.

categories.title: Design, stage management and technical coordination

topics.question: How can lighting guide attention while preserving what performers need to see?
topics.coverage: Compare an original design concept, documented cue intent and visibility constraints; exclude electrical installation or hazardous rigging procedures.

topics.question: What makes a costume functional for a performer as well as meaningful to an audience?
topics.coverage: Examine movement, quick changes, material, maintenance and character information using authorized designs; avoid treating historical silhouette as proof of exact period accuracy.

topics.question: How does a stage manager's prompt book organize a repeatable performance?
topics.coverage: Use a fictional cue extract to connect script location, responsibilities and communication; do not expose a real production's restricted documents.

topics.question: Why can a scene change become part of the production's storytelling?
topics.coverage: Compare visible labor, pace, music and transition imagery in cleared examples; distinguish aesthetic choice from a claim that hidden changes are obsolete.

topics.question: How can a Kathakali episode distinguish public performance analysis from specialist training?
topics.coverage: Use authorized performers' accounts, public repertoire and attributed scholarship on gesture, costume and narrative; avoid teaching restricted or technically demanding practices from clips.

topics.question: What can a Noh performance reveal about convention and audience knowledge?
topics.coverage: Choose an identified play, translation and authorized performance context; explain selected public conventions without treating all Japanese theatre as one form.

topics.question: How do nautanki or tamasha performances relate to their local audiences and changing venues?
topics.coverage: Study one named tradition through consented performers, scripts and historical records; preserve regional variation rather than collapsing folk theatre into a single style.

topics.question: How can a contemporary production draw on classical Indian dramaturgy without claiming direct continuity for every choice?
topics.coverage: Compare an identified public textual concept with the production's own attributed explanation; distinguish inspiration, interpretation and historically demonstrated transmission.

topics.question: How can captioning, audio description and relaxed performances alter access differently?
topics.coverage: Compare services, preparation and consented audience feedback for a named venue; avoid claiming that one access offer meets every person's needs.

topics.question: What changes when theatre is made with a community rather than only about it?
topics.coverage: Trace participation, decision authority, payment, consent and representation; distinguish collaboration from inviting testimony into a predetermined script.

topics.question: Why can ticket price alone fail to explain who attends theatre?
topics.coverage: Investigate transport, timing, language, information and belonging using ethical audience research; avoid treating one venue's attendees as a population sample.

topics.question: What must a touring production change when moving into another venue?
topics.coverage: Map dimensions, crew roles, access, permissions and technical compatibility using authorized riders; exclude unsafe improvisation or assuming the original design fits unchanged.

topics.question: How can a theatre budget distinguish creative ambition from operational commitments?
topics.coverage: Use transparent illustrative costs for rehearsal, rights, staffing, venue and contingency; avoid promising profitability from a full auditorium alone.

topics.question: What rights need checking before recording and distributing a stage performance?
topics.coverage: Review play, music, design, performer and venue permissions under current local rules; distinguish permission to attend from permission to publish footage.

topics.question: How can a reviewer assess an experimental performance without judging it only by conventional plot?
topics.coverage: Identify the work's apparent aims, formal choices and audience relationship using observable evidence; separate personal preference from a claim of objective failure.

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: original engineering papers
official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

community.requirements: Use consented participant accounts, local records and the community's own descriptions. Include differences of position, access and power; testimony is not a representative survey or clinical proof.
source_leads: consented interviews and oral histories
community publications and local records
field notes with method and consent documented

media.requirements: Analyze an identifiable work or create a clearly labeled original example. Connect creative decisions to observable audience information; respect rights, attribution, consent and the difference between intent and reception.
source_leads: the actual work and authorized production materials
creator interviews or published craft explanations
permission-cleared examples and audience feedback

tradition.requirements: Identify the text, edition, translator, commentary, community and ritual context as applicable. Attribute theological and spiritual claims, preserve regional variation and respect public versus restricted knowledge.
source_leads: primary texts in traceable editions
authorized public teaching and ritual descriptions
consented community accounts and critical historical studies

civic.requirements: Use the current official legal text, policy, procedure or public dataset for a specific jurisdiction and date. Distinguish written rules, implementation and lived access; give no personal legal or financial conclusion.
source_leads: official laws, rules and administrative guidance
audits, judgments and public service records
consented accounts from affected people and qualified specialists
